=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (multiple nodes clearly show leaves attached in pairs)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are closely spaced along the short stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (leaves consist of multiple leaflets attached to a central axis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (terminal leaflets are visible at the apex of the leaflets)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 3 (visible leaflets are arranged as a trifoliate group)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): subopposite (leaflets appear paired with a terminal one, though exact symmetry is slightly irregular)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins are smooth without teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are broadly oval, widest near the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tips taper to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf bases are broadly curved)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, moderately spaced, numerous (veins curve slightly towards the margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (surface lacks strong gloss, appears matte)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine, short hairs are visible on the stems and leaf surfaces)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, lacking thick bark)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible on the stem surface)
    19. Stem color: greenish-brown (stems show a mix of green and light brown tones)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no obvious ridges or lenticels are visible)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): not observed (pulvinus is not clearly visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: Some leaflets show minor damage in the form of small holes.
